html:
Hastings Kamuzu Banda was the leader of Malawi from independence in 1964 until 1994, from 1971 as president for life.

He left Nyasaland as a young man, worked in South African mines, and trained as a doctor in the United States and Scotland, practising in Britain for years. He returned in 1958 to lead the campaign against the Federation, was jailed in 1959, and became prime minister and then president.

He ran a one-party state with a youth militia, jailed or killed opponents, enforced strict dress codes, and was the only African leader of his time to have open ties with apartheid South Africa. He moved the capital to Lilongwe. Protests and donor pressure forced the referendum of 1993, and he lost the election of 1994 in Malawi.
